clusters.shared_invariant: Persistence of non-zero mismatch (L0) across all scales.
clusters.tension: Continuous, uniform convergence (ODE/Paper 1) vs. bounded, localized structure (Relational theory Phase Packet).
clusters.pivot_line: The convergent floor is the base state from which Phase Packets emerge when relational multiplicity reaches critical interaction density.
clusters.cluster_pivot: Structural identity is a second-order transition from a continuous relational floor to a discrete bounded packet.

master_pivot.pivot_line: Identity is a threshold phenomenon of interaction reach.
master_pivot.synthesis: The near-floor convergent regime (SS2) identified in Paper 1 is the fundamental ground of the One Process. Phase Packets (SS3) are emergent localizations of this ground that occur strictly when the Interaction Domain (K) and Residue Accumulation Rate (κ) exceed a critical joint threshold (θ_crit). Below this threshold, multiplicity exists but cannot 'lock' into identity.

observations: Floor convergence is a necessary but not sufficient condition for identity.
Phase packets require active boundary formation.
inferred_relationships: Increasing interaction reach (K) at constant residue (κ) will trigger structural localization.
Ablating residue (κ -> 0) will force the system back to the uniform floor regardless of K.
assumptions: The SS2 -> SS3 transition is observable as a qualitative change in spatial/relational variance.
unknowns: The exact numerical value of the θ_crit manifold.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The emergence of discrete Phase Packets (identity) is governed by a critical threshold θ_crit of interaction density; below θ_crit, the system settles into the continuous, uniform near-floor regime (SS2).
predictions: In PDE/CA models, sweeping residue growth (κ) and interaction reach (K) will show a sharp transition from a flat field to a localized structure.
In ABM, increasing agent coupling (Rc) will trigger a phase transition from a uniform swarm (floor) to discrete coherent clusters (identity).
Independent spectral analysis will show a shift from DC-dominant signatures (floor) to complex multi-mode signatures (identity) at the threshold.
hypotheses.falsification_condition: If Phase Packets emerge regardless of coupling/residue levels, or if increasing density fails to trigger localization, the threshold hypothesis is falsified.
